# The Problem

## The Basic Problem at Date $t$ {#MaxProb}

$$
\max_{\cNrm_t,\aNrm_t} \; \Ex_{t}\left[\sum_{n=0}^{T-t}\DiscFac^{n} \uFunc(\cNrm_{t+n})\right]
$$

Labor income: $\yNrm_{t} = \pNrm_{t}\tranShkEmp_{t}$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Rfree_{t}   &= \Rfree \quad \text{constant interest factor} = 1+\rfree \\
\pNrm_{t+1}  &= \PermGroShk_{t+1}\pNrm_{t} \quad \text{permanent labor income dynamics} \\
\log \tranShkEmp_{t+n} &\sim \mathcal{N}(-\sigma_{\tranShkEmp}^{2}/2,\,\sigma_{\tranShkEmp}^{2}) \quad \text{lognormal transitory shocks} \; \forall \; n>0
\end{aligned}
$$

- "Bewley" problem if liquidity constraint, $\PermGroShk_{t+1}$ nonstochastic
- "Friedman/Buffer Stock" problem if also permanent shocks

## Bellman Equation {#vrecurse}

$$
\vLevBF_{t}(\mLvl_{t},\pLvl_{t}) = \max_{\cLvl_{t}} \; \uFunc(\cLvl_{t}) + \Ex_{t}[\DiscFac \; \vLevBF_{t+1}(\mLvl_{t+1},\pLvl_{t+1})]
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mLvl &\;-\; \text{"market resources" (net worth plus current income)} \\
\pLvl &\;-\; \text{permanent labor income}
\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
\uFunc(\cNrm) = \left(\frac{\cNrm^{1-\CRRA}}{1-\CRRA}\right)
$$

## Normalize the Problem {#Normalize}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vFunc_{t}(\mNrm_{t}) &= \max_{\cNrm_{t},\aNrm_t} \;\; \uFunc(\cNrm_{t})+
        \DiscFac \Ex_{t}[\PermGroShk_{t+1}^{1-\CRRA}\vFunc_{t+1}(\mNrm_{t+1})] \\
&\text{s.t.} \\
\aNrm_{t}   &= \mNrm_{t}-\cNrm_{t} \\
\mNrm_{t+1} &= \underbrace{\left(\Rfree/\PermGroShk_{t+1}\right)}_{\equiv \Rnorm_{t+1}}\aNrm_{t}+\tranShkEmp_{t+1}
\end{aligned}
$$

where nonbold variables are bold ones normalized by $\pLvl$:

$$
\mNrm_{t} = \mLvl_{t}/\pLvl_{t}
$$

$\Rightarrow$ $\cFunc_{t}(\mNrm)$ from which we can obtain

$$
\cLvl_{t}(\mLvl_{t},\pLvl_{t}) = \cFunc_{t}(\mLvl_{t}/\pLvl_{t})\pLvl_{t}
$$

## My First Notational Atrocity

. . .

...in this paper.

. . .

$$
\vEnd_{t}(\aNrm_{t}) = \Ex_{t}[\DiscFac \PermGroShk_{t+1}^{1-\CRRA}\vFunc_{t+1}(\Rnorm_{t+1} \aNrm_{t}+\tranShkEmp_{t+1})]
$$

so FOC is

$$
\uPrime(\cNrm_{t}) = \vEnd_{t}^{\prime}(\mNrm_{t}-\cNrm_{t})
$$

or

$$
\cNrm_{t}^{-\CRRA} = \vEnd_{t}^{\prime}(\aNrm_{t})
$$

## The Method of Endogenous Gridpoints

. . .

- Define vector of *end-of-period* asset values $\vec{\aNrm}$
- For each $\aNrm[j]$ compute $\vEnd_{t}^{\prime}(\aNrm[j])$

. . .

Each of these $\vEnd_{t}^{\prime}[j]$ corresponds to a unique $\cNrm[j]$ via FOC:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cNrm[j]^{-\CRRA} &= \vEnd_{t}^{\prime}(\aNrm[j]) \\
\cNrm[j] &= \left(\vEnd_{t}^{\prime}(\aNrm[j])\right)^{-1/\CRRA}
\end{aligned}
$$

## The Method of Endogenous Gridpoints (cont.)

But the DBC says

$$
\begin{aligned}
\aNrm_{t} &= \mNrm_{t} - \cNrm_{t} \\
\mNrm[j]  &= \aNrm[j] + \cNrm[j]
\end{aligned}
$$

. . .

So computing $\vEnd_{t}^{\prime}$ at a vector of $\vec{\aNrm}$ values (easy) has produced for us the corresponding $\vec{\cNrm}$ and $\vec{\mNrm}$ values at virtually no cost!

. . .

From these we can interpolate to construct $\grave{\cFunc}_{t}(\mNrm)$.

# The Method of Moderation

## The Optimist, the Pessimist, and the Realist

Call the "true" problem that of a "realist"

. . .

Contrasts with:

. . .

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Optimist} &: \text{Believes } \tranShkEmp_{t+n} = \overbrace{1}^{=\Ex_{t}[\tranShkEmp_{t+n}]} \; \forall \; n>0, \text{ consumes } \cFuncOpt_{t} \\
\text{Pessimist} &: \text{Believes } \tranShkEmp_{t+n} = \tranShkEmpMin \; \forall \; n>0, \text{ consumes } \cFuncPes_{t}
\end{aligned}
$$

. . .

Useful because:

1. Both of these are perfect foresight problems
   - Linear analytical solution (easy!)
2. $\cFuncPes_{t} < \cFunc_{t} < \cFuncOpt_{t}$

## Definitions and Solutions for Perfect Foresight Problem

$$
\begin{aligned}
\MPCmin_{t} &: \text{MPC for perfect foresight problem in period } t \\
\hNrmOpt_{t}   &: \text{end-of-period-}t\text{ human wealth for "optimist"} \\
\hNrmPes_{t} &: \text{end-of-period-}t\text{ human wealth for "pessimist"}
\end{aligned}
$$

- Pessimist's solution:
$$
\cFuncPes_{t}(\mNrm) = \underbrace{(\mNrm + \hNrmPes_{t})}_{\equiv \mNrmEx} \MPCmin_{t}
$$

- Optimist's solution:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\cFuncOpt_{t}(\mNrm) &= (\mNrm + \hNrmOpt_{t}) \MPCmin_{t} \\
&= \cFuncPes_{t}(\mNrm) + \underbrace{(\hNrmOpt_{t}-\hNrmPes_{t})}_{\equiv \hNrmEx_{t}} \MPCmin_{t}
\end{aligned}
$$

## Key Inequalities

$$
\begin{array}{rcl}
\mNrmEx_{t} \MPCmin_{t} < & \cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t}) & < (\mNrmEx_{t}+\hNrmEx_{t})\MPCmin_{t} \\[4pt]
-\mNrmEx_{t} \MPCmin_{t} > & -\cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t}) & > -(\mNrmEx_{t}+\hNrmEx_{t})\MPCmin_{t} \\[4pt]
\hNrmEx_{t} \MPCmin_{t} > & \cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t})-\cFuncPes_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t}) & > 0 \\[4pt]
1 > & \underbrace{\left(\dfrac{\cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t})-\cFuncPes_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t})}{\hNrmEx_{t} \MPCmin_{t}}\right)}_{\equiv \modRte_{t}} & > 0
\end{array}
$$

Defining $\logmNrmEx_{t} = \log \mNrmEx_{t}$ (which can range from $-\infty$ to $\infty$), the moderation ratio is

$$
\modRte_{t}(\logmNrmEx_{t}) \equiv \left(\frac{\cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+e^{\logmNrmEx_{t}})-\cFuncPes_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+e^{\logmNrmEx_{t}})}{\hNrmEx_{t} \MPCmin_{t}}\right)
$$

and we now define (positive-logit convention)

$$
\logitModRte_{t}(\logmNrmEx_{t}) = \log \left(\frac{\modRte_{t}(\logmNrmEx_{t})}{1-\modRte_{t}(\logmNrmEx_{t})}\right)
$$

## Approximating Precautionary Saving

$$
\cFuncReal_{t} = \cFuncPes_{t}+\overbrace{\frac{1}{1+\exp(-\logitModRte_{t})}}^{=\modRte_{t}} \hNrmEx_{t} \MPCmin_{t}
$$

In the limit as $\logmNrmEx$ approaches either $\infty$ or $-\infty$ this gives the "right" answer.

## Solving for the Value Function

Given analytical object

$$
\mathbb{C}_{t}^{T} \equiv \mathrm{PDV}_{t}^{T}(\cNrm)/\cNrm_{t}
$$

The perfect foresight value function is:

$$
\vFunc_{t}(\mNrm_{t}) = \uFunc(\cNrm_{t})\mathbb{C}_{t}^{T}
$$

which can be transformed as

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vInv_{t} &\equiv \left((1-\CRRA)\vFunc_{t}\right)^{1/(1-\CRRA)} \\
&= \cNrm_{t}(\mathbb{C}_{t}^{T})^{1/(1-\CRRA)}
\end{aligned}
$$

In the limit as $\logmNrmEx$ approaches either $\infty$ or $-\infty$ this gives the "right" answer.

## Approximate Inverted Value Function

Same steps as for consumption function, because

$$
\vFuncPes_{t} < \vFunc_{t} < \vFuncOpt_{t}
$$

Produce

$$
\Alt{\vFunc}_{t}(\mNrm) = \uFunc(\Alt{\vInv}_{t}(\mNrm))
$$

# A Refinement

## A Tighter Limit: $\cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrm) < \min[\MPCmax_{t} \mNrmEx_{t},\, \cFuncOpt_{t}(\mNrm_{t})]$

![](images/IntExpFOCInvPesReaOptNeed45Plot.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

## The Tighter Upper Bound

We want to construct a consumption function for $\mNrm_{t} \in (\mNrmMin_{t}, \mNrm_{t}^{\#}]$ that respects the tighter upper bound:

$$
\begin{array}{rcl}
\mNrmEx_{t} \MPCmin_{t} < & \cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t}) & < \MPCmax_{t} \mNrmEx_{t} \\[4pt]
\mNrmEx_{t}(\MPCmax_{t}-\MPCmin_{t}) > & \MPCmax_{t} \mNrmEx_{t}-\cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t}) & > 0 \\[4pt]
1 > & \left(\dfrac{\MPCmax_{t} \mNrmEx_{t}-\cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+\mNrmEx_{t})}{\mNrmEx_{t}(\MPCmax_{t}-\MPCmin_{t})}\right) & > 0
\end{array}
$$

Again defining $\logmNrmEx_{t} = \log \mNrmEx_{t}$, the low-resource moderation ratio is

$$
\modRteLoTightUpBd_{t}(\logmNrmEx_{t}) \equiv \frac{\MPCmax_{t}-\cFuncReal_{t}(\mNrmMin_{t}+e^{\logmNrmEx_{t}})e^{-\logmNrmEx_{t}}}{\MPCmax_{t}-\MPCmin_{t}}
$$

## Combining Old and New Functions

Defining indicator functions

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{1}_{\text{Lo}}(\mNrm) &= 1 \text{ if } \mNrm \leq \bar{\check{\mNrm}}_{t}^{\#} \\
\mathbf{1}_{\text{Mid}}(\mNrm) &= 1 \text{ if } \bar{\check{\mNrm}}_{t}^{\#} < \mNrm < \underline{\hat{\mNrm}}_{t}^{\#} \\
\mathbf{1}_{\text{Hi}}(\mNrm)  &= 1 \text{ if } \underline{\hat{\mNrm}}_{t}^{\#} \leq \mNrm
\end{aligned}
$$

we can define a well-behaved approximating consumption function

$$
\Alt{\cFunc}_{t} = \mathbf{1}_{\text{Lo}} \Alt{\Lo{\cFunc}}_{t} + \mathbf{1}_{\text{Mid}} \Alt{\tilde{\cFunc}}_{t}+\mathbf{1}_{\text{Hi}} \Alt{\Hi{\cFunc}}_{t}
$$

# An Extension

## Extension To Case With Financial Risk Too

$$
\log \Risky_{t+n} \sim \mathcal{N}(\rfree + \equityPrem - \sigma^{2}_{\risky}/2,\,\sigma^{2}_{\risky}) \; \forall \; n>0
$$

[@Merton1969] and [@Samuelson1969]: Without labor income,

$$
\MPC = 1- \left(\DiscFac \; \Ex_{t}[\Risky_{t+1}^{1-\CRRA}]\right)^{1/\CRRA}
$$

and in this case the previous analysis applies once we substitute this MPC for the one that characterizes the perfect foresight problem without rate-of-return risk.

# Conclusions

## How Useful Is It?

When it works:

- Can approximate solution *globally* with very few gridpoints
- Can speed solution substantially

. . .

When Might It Not Work?

- Consumption With Nonconvexities
- Problems With No Perfect Foresight Solution
  - How Many Such Problems Have A Solution With Shocks?
- *Should* Work For Value Functions Fairly Generally
